observation.visible_scene: A night-sky fireworks burst centered in the frame, with a small static blue-and-red logo overlay fixed in the top-left corner throughout. The burst consists of a bright central core, an inner ring of fine radial streaks, and fainter outer tendrils; the dark background shows no other objects.
visible_changes: The central core stays near the same image position (roughly frame center) for the whole excerpt while the surrounding streaks lengthen radially outward, indicating expansion of the burst rather than translation of the whole object.

The color of the inner radial streaks shifts over time: deep red (frames 1–6) → orange/gold (frames 7–9) → gold with a green glow forming around the core (frames 10–13) → stronger green ring (frames 14–23) → green fades and gold dominates again (frames 24–30).
A green halo appears around the white core mid-excerpt and later dissipates, while the core itself dims from a saturated white to a softer yellow-white cloud.
Faint reddish outer tendrils visible early on fade out by the middle of the clip.
From about frame 24 onward, small violet/purple points emerge at the outer tips of the long radial streaks and become increasingly prominent, tracing a large spherical outline by frames 31–41.
The overall diameter of the bright streak field grows steadily from frame 1 to frame 41.
The top-left logo remains pixel-locked in place across all frames, consistent with a static camera (no evident pan or zoom).
outside_clip_unknowns: The launch, ascent, or burst trigger of the firework shell before t=0 is not shown.
The trajectory, falling, and final fade-out of the sparks after t=2.667s are not shown.
The physical composition of the color-changing stars is not determinable from the images.
uncertain_details: Whether the slight apparent shift of the burst center is real motion or camera jitter cannot be confirmed from the dark background alone.
The exact moment each color transition begins is gradual and frame-rate limited, so boundaries between color phases are approximate.

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
